stories.title: Texas halts new data center grid connections as demand overwhelms power system
stories.summary: Texas has paused new data center connections to its power grid, citing overwhelming demand from the AI buildout. The state's governor has ordered audits of new data center projects after officials tallied more than 400 gigawatts of requested capacity — far beyond what the grid can currently support.
stories.whyItMatters: Texas has been a magnet for AI data center construction, so a connection freeze there signals that grid capacity, not chip supply or capital, may become the next bottleneck for the AI buildout.
whatToWatch: Results of the governor's ordered audit of pending data center projects
Whether other grid operators follow Texas with similar pauses or reviews
How affected data center developers and AI companies respond publicly
questions: How long will the connection halt last, and which projects get grandfathered in?
Does 400+ gigawatts of requested capacity reflect real near-term demand or speculative reservations?

stories.title: Apple says more ex-employees may have taken trade secrets to OpenAI
stories.summary: Apple has expanded its claims in its trade secrets litigation, saying additional former employees beyond those already named may have carried confidential information to OpenAI. OpenAI has pushed back, characterizing Apple's lawsuit as "aggressive and oddly personal."
stories.whyItMatters: The dispute highlights rising tension between Apple and OpenAI even as the two work together on AI features, and underscores how fiercely talent and trade secrets are being contested in the AI race.
whatToWatch: Whether Apple names additional former employees or expands the lawsuit's scope
OpenAI's formal legal response to the amended claims
Any impact on Apple and OpenAI's existing product partnership
questions: What specific confidential material does Apple allege was taken?
Is this litigation strategy or a genuine trade-secrets concern?

stories.title: Signal now lets you securely link multiple phones to one account
stories.summary: Signal has rolled out a feature allowing users to securely link multiple phones to a single account, expanding beyond its previous linked-device model that mostly served desktop and tablet companions.
stories.whyItMatters: For a privacy-focused messenger widely used by journalists, activists, and security-conscious users, multi-phone support removes a long-standing usability limitation without compromising Signal's encryption model.
whatToWatch: User adoption and feedback on the new multi-device linking flow
questions: Are there limits on how many phones can be linked at once?

stories.title: SpaceX's first public earnings show it now makes more from AI than from space
stories.summary: In its first public earnings disclosure, SpaceX reported that revenue tied to AI-related business now exceeds revenue from its traditional space operations, such as launch and Starlink. The figures paint a company whose financial profile increasingly resembles an AI firm rather than a pure aerospace company.
stories.whyItMatters: SpaceX has long been valued as a space and satellite-internet company; a shift toward AI-driven revenue could reshape how investors and regulators view its business and its ties to the broader AI infrastructure boom.
whatToWatch: Further detail on what specific AI business lines are driving the revenue
Whether SpaceX continues public earnings disclosures going forward
Reaction from investors and competitors in both the space and AI sectors

stories.whyItMatters: As automakers increasingly treat in-car displays as software platforms, this test case shows how far carmakers may push advertising into spaces customers already paid for, a trend likely to spark backlash across the industry.

stories.whyItMatters: AMD's shift mirrors a broader industry pattern of chipmakers prioritizing AI data center demand over consumer hardware, with implications for pricing and availability across both markets.

stories.title: Android app developers may be unwittingly leaking users' location data to advertisers
stories.summary: A report indicates that some Android app developers may be inadvertently sharing users' location data with advertising networks, likely through embedded software development kits (SDKs) whose data-sharing practices developers themselves may not fully understand.
stories.whyItMatters: The finding points to a structural privacy risk in the mobile app ecosystem, where third-party SDKs can move sensitive data beyond what developers or users intend or consent to.
whatToWatch: Whether Google responds with policy changes or SDK restrictions
Whether specific apps or ad networks are named and face scrutiny
questions: Which SDKs or ad networks are responsible for the unintended sharing?

stories.title: More AI agent hacking incidents are surfacing

stories.whyItMatters: As companies rush to deploy AI agents that can take actions on users' behalf, a mounting pattern of hacking incidents raises questions about whether security safeguards are keeping pace with agent capabilities.
